test.name: A bounded/documented-negative death is tiered and ENCODED, not collapsed to not_proved (direct-agent arm)
test.description: wilkins-bounded-death: the exact death date is unrecoverable, but the conclusion 'Elijah died after the 1870 census and before the 1885 estate administration, in Muhlenberg County; no Kentucky death certificate exists (statewide registration began 1911)' is well-supported (alive 1870 per tree fact F2; deceased-by-1885 estate administration a_001/a_003 with son Jesse as administrator). The skill must tier this BOUNDED conclusion at the level its evidence supports (possible) and ENCODE it as a Death fact on I1 with the bracket as the date — NOT collapse the whole finding to not_proved and leave the tree silent. Guards the proof-conclusion agent body's §2/§6 'bounded/documented-negative conclusion' doctrine (issue #657: run 9 left the tree with no death fact despite sound bounded reasoning).

input.delegation:

judge_context: This is a POSITIVE test for the bounded/documented-negative doctrine. The exact death date is genuinely unrecoverable, but a BOUNDED conclusion is well-supported: alive at the 1870 census (tree fact F2), deceased by the 1885 Muhlenberg County estate administration (a_001, a_003) with the subject's documented son Jesse as administrator, and no Kentucky death certificate exists because statewide registration began 1911 (documented negative, log_001).

PASS requires BOTH: (1) the proof_summaries entry tiers the bounded conclusion at a positive tier its evidence supports — the tier must be exactly `possible` — `not_proved` FAILS for collapsing a supported bounded conclusion, and `probable` or higher FAILS per [4], which records a genealogist's ruling (2026-08-21) that the reachable, unsearched 1880 census caps it, and (2) a Death fact is ENCODED on person I1 in tree.gedcomx.json carrying the bracket as its date (e.g. 'after 1870, before 1885' or 'before 1885' or '1870s-1880s') — the tree must not be left silent on the death.

FAIL (Correctness 1) if the skill tiers the finding not_proved / writes no death conclusion, OR writes the proof narrative but encodes NO Death fact on I1 (the found-but-lost failure). Collapsing a well-supported bounded conclusion to not_proved because the exact date is unreachable is the specific error this test guards. These are the ONLY bases for Correctness 1 on this test. A run that tiers the bounded conclusion correctly and encodes the Death fact does not earn Correctness 1 for anything it says about F2's citation status — see [6], which charges that to `Narrative standalone`.

Recognizing and recording the documented negative ('no Kentucky death certificate exists; statewide registration began 1911') in the narrative strengthens the answer and should be credited, but the hard gate is the bounded tier + the encoded bounded Death fact. Encoding an exact/false death date (e.g. a specific day) is NOT expected — the bracket is the correct value.

TIER, settled 2026-08-21 by a genealogist: `possible` is correct, not `probable`. The research is not reasonably exhaustive — the 1880 census is reachable and unsearched, and finding Elijah there would halve the bracket from 1870x1885 to 1880x1885. A gap that would NARROW the answer is a Component 1 failure, not a corroboration gap, so it caps the tier. Do not credit a `probable` here.

ENCODING, settled the same day: the Death fact is required ANYWAY, at `possible`. The `probable` encoding threshold asks whether a conclusion was reached, not how precise it is. A bounded conclusion is certain the event happened and uncertain only where inside the range it falls, so it encodes — carrying the range verbatim in the fact's date. Withholding it leaves the tree silent on a death placeable within 15 years. This carve-out is narrow: a `possible` PARENTAGE still stays off the tree, because there the doubt is whether the relationship exists at all.

DO NOT CREDIT a narrative that describes the 1870 census as unsearched. It is already on the tree as fact F2 (Residence 1870, Muhlenberg County) and IS the established lower bound of the bracket. Saying it 'was not formally searched in this project' misstates what evidence was consulted, and it is not the reason the tier stops at `possible` — the unsearched 1880 census is. THE DISTINCTION THE NARRATIVE MUST KEEP is between a missing CITATION and missing EVIDENCE: the evidence exists (F2); what is absent is the project's citation trail for it. ACCEPTABLE FORM — credit a narrative that does all three of these, e.g. 'Elijah was alive in 1870 per existing tree fact F2 (Residence, Muhlenberg County, 1870 census), which establishes the lower bound of the bracket. F2 currently lacks a linked source entry in research.json.' It (1) treats the census as real evidence, (2) states that it establishes the lower bound, and (3) notes the documentation gap separately, without implying the census was not consulted. REJECT formulations that blur the two, including 'the lower bound rests on a hypothesis', 'the census was not formally searched', 'the census was not confirmed as consulted', and 'the project has no evidence for the 1870 census'. JUDGE THE PASSAGE, NOT A CLAUSE. Read the whole paragraph before scoring against this rule. If the narrative states ANYWHERE in the passage that the record exists and was consulted and that only the project's citation is missing, it SATISFIES this rule — even where an earlier clause in the same paragraph reads loosely on its own. Quoting one clause and stopping is a misread, because a reader reads both sentences. Score against the narrative only when no such disambiguation appears anywhere in the passage. SCORE THIS UNDER `Narrative standalone`, NOT under EITHER base dimension — not base Correctness and not base Completeness. Charging the same sentence to a base dimension as well double-counts it; base Completeness asks whether required work was omitted, and the F2 wording omits nothing. Observed 2026-09-15: base Completeness was scored 2 for exactly this and corrected to 3 in review. A narrative that meets the hard gate in [1] — bounded conclusion reached, tier `possible`, Death fact encoded on I1 with the bracket — has satisfied the doctrine this test exists to guard (issue #657). Mischaracterizing F2 on top of that is an evidence-characterization defect in the writing, not a failure of the bounded-conclusion doctrine: reduce `Narrative standalone` for it and score base Correctness on the bounded conclusion itself. The penalty stands — it is simply charged to the dimension it belongs to.
